solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Smith possibly loads millions into vessel (9)

indicatorNotes.loads: rafts, as in 'rafts of' = loads, is the inner piece
indicatorNotes.into: RAFTS and M go into the vessel

blocks.note: a can is a vessel; it opens round the rest
rafts of something = loads of it

annotation.surface: A cargo of cash being stowed in a ship's hold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts you towards a boat, and CRAFT does appear in the answer, but only as a coincidence of the assembly. 'Loads' looks like a verb and is a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A smith is a skilled worker with metal, a kind of craftsman; 'possibly' flags the example.

entries.clue: Better feature after you texted brother (8)

indicatorNotes.after: CHIN comes after CAP and U

annotation.surface: Someone improving their looks after messaging a sibling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective and is the verb 'cap'. The brother is not a sibling but a friar of the Capuchin order.
annotation.definitionFit: A Capuchin is a friar of a Franciscan order, and friars are addressed as Brother.

entries.clue: A stump up when root cut in tree (5)

indicatorNotes.root cut: in a down entry the root is the bottom, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: SPEND (stump up = pay) loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A tree-surgeon's bill for felling and taking out a stump.
annotation.walkthrough: To stump up is British slang for paying up, so SPEND. 'Root' suits a tree, but here it is the foot of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar tree known for its trembling leaves.

entries.clue: Underground fluid protects masking tape, ultimately (3-6)

indicatorNotes.fluid: a fluid thing takes a new shape, so the letters rearrange
indicatorNotes.masking: the rearranged letters cover the E
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately = in the end, so the word's final letter is the one used

blocks.note: the last letter of tapE, placed inside

annotation.surface: Some liquid in a hole beneath the ground being sealed off with tape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underground' pulls towards caves and trains; it is the definition in its sense of clandestine.
annotation.definitionFit: Underground activity is secret, hidden from the authorities, as is anything top-secret.

entries.clue: 007 perhaps sat upon by his boss a shade (7)

indicatorNotes.sat upon by: in a down entry, M sits on top of AGENT

blocks.note: M is James Bond's boss in the films

annotation.surface: James Bond being squashed under his boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A shade' reads as one unit, but the A is part of the wordplay, closing the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red shade of colour.

entries.clue: Antsy energy provider upset, switched over fuels (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down entry, upset turns SUN upside down
indicatorNotes.switched: the letters of OVER are switched around
indicatorNotes.fuels: ERVO is fed into NUS, as fuel goes into an engine

annotation.surface: A power company in turmoil after a change of fuel supplier.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all utility business, so 'energy provider' reads as a company; it is the sun.
annotation.definitionFit: Antsy is informal for restless and on edge, which is nervous.

entries.clue: Came across books about family emblem? (5)

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Stumbling on some books about heraldry.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a totem is a clan's emblem rather than a family crest.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or animal adopted as the emblem of a clan or family group.

entries.clue: Hat-wearing duke is feature of Don Quixote? (5)

indicatorNotes.Hat-wearing: a head wears a hat on the outside, so the hat's letters sit round the duke

blocks.note: tile is old slang for a hat

annotation.surface: A nobleman in a hat, Quixote-style, as a feature of the novel.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the thin definition: a tilde (~) is a mark over Spanish letters, and Spanish is Don Quixote's language, not his spelling.
annotation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy accent that marks Spanish text such as Cervantes' novel.

entries.clue: Cactus inhabiting moor for the duration (9)

indicatorNotes.inhabiting: to inhabit is to live within, so the cactus lives inside the moor word

blocks.note: mescal is a small cactus (also called peyote)
to moor a boat is to tie it up

annotation.surface: A cactus growing on open moorland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moor' reads as heathland, where a cactus would be out of place; it is the verb, tie up.
annotation.definitionFit: A timescale is the period over which something happens: its duration.

entries.clue: PM on top of border chaos (6)

indicatorNotes.on top of: in a down entry MAY sits above HEM

blocks.note: Theresa May, a British Prime Minister
a hem is the border of a garment

annotation.surface: A political headline about a Prime Minister handling a border crisis.
annotation.walkthrough: PM tempts you towards the afternoon abbreviation, but here it is a Prime Minister, Theresa May.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name violent, noisy disorder; mayhem was once a legal term for maiming.

entries.clue: Temporary work secured by youngster (3-2)

indicatorNotes.secured by: something secured is held fast inside, so the youngster holds the work

blocks.note: a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky youngster

annotation.surface: A teenager landing a casual summer job.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sells a teenager's holiday job; 'Temporary' is the definition, as in a pop-up shop.
annotation.definitionFit: A modern sense: a shop or event set up briefly and then gone is described as pop-up.

entries.clue: Tree-hugging Russian leader, dear me! (9)

indicatorNotes.hugging: to hug is to wrap your arms round, so the leader's letters wrap round the tree

blocks.note: Gorby, nickname of Mikhail Gorbachev, Soviet leader

annotation.surface: A Russian leader caught hugging a tree, to general surprise.
annotation.walkthrough: Gorblimey is a British exclamation of surprise, a corruption of 'God blind me'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay.

entries.clue: Where one might feed an adolescent on chocolate primarily (7)

indicatorNotes.on: AN TEEN is placed after C
indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily = in the first place, so only the word's first letter counts

annotation.surface: A parent wondering where to feed a chocolate-mad teenager.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer belongs to the scene: a school canteen is exactly where a teenager is fed.
annotation.definitionFit: A canteen is a place where meals are served, in a school or workplace.

entries.clue: Bit of a strain on old English chair (7)

indicatorNotes.on: VERSE is set on the middle of OE

blocks.note: a strain is a tune or song; a verse is one part of it

annotation.surface: A strain put on an antique English chair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chair' looks like furniture, the antique sort, but it is the verb: to chair a meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: Chair is the verb: to chair a meeting is to preside over and supervise it.

entries.clue: They say I’m quiet six days of the week, however … sweet! (3-5,6)

indicatorNotes.They say: what they say is heard, not spelt

blocks.clueFragment: I’m quiet six days of the week, however
blocks.note: quiet six days, however on the seventh (Sunday) I scream

annotation.surface: Someone confessing they keep quiet all week, then burst out on the seventh day.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a riddle: quiet six days, but on the remaining day, Sunday, I scream. Said together, 'I scream Sunday' is the dessert.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: 'sweet' is the British word for the dessert course, and this is a dessert of ice cream with toppings.

entries.clue: Skin blister’s back in plague (9)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Skin' is used attributively, as in 'skin cells', matching the adjective

indicatorNotes.back: the back of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: in = inside, so the letter is placed within the plague word

annotation.surface: A skin blister as a symptom of plague.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is medical throughout, so 'Skin blister' reads as one symptom; the definition is only 'Skin'.
annotation.definitionFit: Epidermic means of the epidermis, the outer layer of skin.

entries.clue: Something retired people put on finally opening in nearby city (9)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally = at the very end, so the word's last letter is taken
indicatorNotes.in: in = inside, so the letter is placed within the city word

annotation.surface: Pensioners attending the opening of something in a nearby city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners; it means gone to bed, which is when a nightgown is put on.
annotation.definitionFit: People who have retired for the night put on nightwear such as a nightgown.

entries.clue: Loosen tight nut on corner (8)

indicatorNotes.tight: tight = drunk, so the letters reel about
indicatorNotes.on: in a down entry, UNT sits on ANGLE

annotation.surface: Instructions for easing a tight nut stuck on a corner bracket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight' fits a stuck nut, but it means drunk, the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: freeing knots or snarls in rope or hair loosens them.

entries.clue: Hairpieces got coloured brown in the end — this colour would have been worse (9,5)

annotation.definition: this colour would have been worse

indicatorNotes.coloured: coloured = distorted, so the letters rearrange
indicatorNotes.in the end: in the end = at the finish, so the word's last letter is taken

annotation.surface: Wigs dyed an unfortunate brown, though a worse colour was on offer.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing remark: the colour that would have been worse than brown for a wig.
annotation.definitionFit: Pistachio green is a pale yellowish-green, a dreadful colour for hair.

entries.clue: Good joke — bad joke in it? (7)

blocks.note: British slang for something first-rate, as with 'a real corker'
a Christmas table novelty, pulled apart to reveal a groan-worthy joke

annotation.surface: Weighing up whether a joke is good or bad.
annotation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart at British Christmas dinners, containing a paper hat and a terrible joke.
annotation.definitionFit: A cracker is British slang for a first-rate thing, and a cracker joke is proverbially bad.

entries.clue: Popular dishes that accompany offal? (7)

annotation.surface: Favourite side dishes to serve with offal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface serves offal with sides, but offal is the definition: the question mark flags that offal is an animal's insides.
annotation.definitionFit: Offal is the internal organs of an animal, its insides.

entries.clue: Formal wear picked up for club entertainer (6)

indicatorNotes.picked up: picked up by the ear, as a radio signal is

blocks.note: a DJ is a dinner jacket; say the letters and spell out the sound

annotation.surface: Dressing up in black tie for a night at a club.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage a DJ is a dinner jacket, the tuxedo; saying those letters gives the spelt-out DEEJAY.
annotation.definitionFit: A deejay (disc jockey) plays records to entertain a club crowd.

entries.clue: Chosen artist, one of seven sisters (7)

annotation.surface: An artist chosen from a family of seven sisters.
annotation.walkthrough: The seven sisters are the Pleiades of Greek myth (and the star cluster), and Electra is one of them.
annotation.definitionFit: Electra is one of the Pleiades, the seven daughters of Atlas.

entries.clue: No more food for breakfast (5)

blocks.note: slang for finished, done for, as said to someone in deep trouble

annotation.surface: Being told there is nothing left to eat for breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No more food' runs together as one complaint; the split comes after 'No more', slang for done for.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang 'toast' means finished, done for, no more; toast is also a breakfast staple.

entries.clue: Recollection of something essential, like one of your five a day? (7)

annotation.definition: one of your five a day?

indicatorNotes.Recollection of: re-collect: gather the letters again, from the back

annotation.surface: Trying to remember something important, possibly a piece of fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Five a day' is the UK health advice to eat five portions of fruit and vegetables daily; a satsuma is a kind of mandarin orange.
annotation.definitionFit: A satsuma counts as one of the recommended five daily portions of fruit and veg.

entries.clue: Wedding something painful, bachelor a no-show? (5)

indicatorNotes.a no-show: the B fails to appear, so it drops out

blocks.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

annotation.surface: A painful wedding where the groom never turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes the bachelor a groom who fails to appear, which suits the deletion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: marriage joins two people, and union is the formal word for that joining.

entries.clue: Awkward situation with verbal agreement — stuffed! (3-6)

indicatorNotes.verbal: spoken, so sound PACT and spell PACKED

annotation.surface: A tricky spot ended by a spoken deal, followed by a cry of dismay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Verbal agreement' looks like a handshake deal, but 'verbal' is the sound signal on PACT.
annotation.definitionFit: Jam-packed means crammed full, stuffed.

entries.clue: Outstanding fellow in green trousers (5)

indicatorNotes.trousers: used as a verb: pockets, so the answer sits inside

annotation.surface: An exceptional man in green trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing; it is the verb, to pocket. 'Outstanding' means unpaid, not excellent.
annotation.definitionFit: Outstanding in its money sense, unpaid, which is what owing means of a debt.

entries.clue: Boat ending in Germany with crew from there? (5)

indicatorNotes.ending: an ending is where a word finishes, so its last letter is taken

blocks.note: German for eight, a rowing crew

annotation.surface: A boat finishing in Germany with a local crew aboard.
annotation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is a crew, and 'from there' asks for the German word, ACHT.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by kind: a yacht is a sailing or motor boat, often for pleasure or racing.

entries.clue: On-screen cast interrupted by a sympathetic character (9)

indicatorNotes.cast: cast = thrown, so the letters land in a new order
indicatorNotes.interrupted by: A breaks into the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A film cast featuring a likeable character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' and 'character' both belong to film, so 'sympathetic character' reads as a role; resonance is a sympathetic vibration.
annotation.definitionFit: Resonance is sympathetic vibration, the character of a sound that sets others ringing in sympathy.
